plot: On Monday morning Mom finds a black face drawn on her Thanksgiving pumpkin and blames Mia, and everyone looks at sooty Crispy; Detective Zeek proves Mia has no black crayon and Crispy's soot smears while the lines don't, but the tiny numbers along the smile lead to the twist — the detective did it: Zeek's black fingertips (planted early) came from measuring the pumpkin for the window with a burnt matchstick in the dark; he confesses over the walkie, Mia reads the numbers to Mom, it fits the window exactly and Mia is praised — then Uncle Gus says Mia must ride her bike without training wheels on Thursday, and she can't.

script.title: Who Drew a Face on Mom's Pumpkin?

beats.say: Mom found a black face on her Thanksgiving pumpkin!
And she thinks Mia did it. No parade for Mia!
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Monday morning. The big pumpkin sits on the counter, ready for Thursday.
Two black circles for eyes. One long, curvy line for a smile.
B-black lines. Black like... soot.
Slowly, everyone turns to look at Crispy.
Of course. Something turns black. It must be the burnt one.
Nobody is guilty without evidence. Detective Zeek takes the case!
Zeek, why are your fingertips black?
Pencil dust. I was up late with my measuring tape.
Clue one: the lines are perfectly neat. Way too neat for crayons.
Mia's crayons are all bright anyway. She has no black one.
It's true. Forty crayons in the pencil case. Not a single black.
Then we tell Mom. Somehow. Before Mia loses the parade.
At nine, Mia must say sorry. For something she didn't do.
And if it wasn't Mia, who's left? Me.
Then we test you. Science clears names, Crispy.
Zeek lays a white paper napkin on the floor. Test number one.
Crispy, roll across it. Slowly. Like you would on a pumpkin.
Crispy rolls. The napkin turns black. Smudgy. Messy. Everywhere.
Smudges! Crispy's soot smears. The pumpkin lines don't smear at all.
So Crispy's innocent? Hooray! Wait. Then who is guilty?
Innocent. Nobody has ever said that word about me.
The kitchen clock ticks. Eight forty. Twenty minutes left.
Maybe a burglar? A pumpkin burglar with a marker?
A burglar who breaks in to draw a smile? Cutest burglar ever.
Clue two. Look closer. Tiny numbers along the smile.
Very small. Very neat. Thirty-one. Fifteen and a half. Ninety-seven.
Who writes math on a pumpkin? That's so w-weird.
Everyone looks at the one bro who writes math on everything.
No. Impossible. I would remember. I have a perfect memory.
Zeek looks at his black fingertips. Then at a burnt matchstick.
Oh no. Last night. The lights were off. I was measuring.
Mom asked if the pumpkin fits in the window. I checked.
With a burnt matchstick as my pencil. In the dark.
The eyes mark the width. The smile is my measuring curve.
Zeek. You let Crispy take the blame. For ten whole minutes.
Ten minutes is nothing. I'm used to it. Go fix it.
Eight fifty-five. Footsteps. Mia comes down the stairs, head low.
Five minutes, Zeek! Mia is saying sorry for your math!
Then I say sorry first. The walkie! Quick!
Zeek jumps on the walkie button with both feet.
Mia, it was me. Tell Mom to read the numbers. Over.
Mia turns the pumpkin around and reads the tiny numbers to Mom.
Thirty-one wide. The window is thirty-two. It fits. Exactly.
Mom blinks. You measured it for me? That's my smart girl.
A friend helped, Mia says. She winks at the bread box.
Crispy, I'm sorry. Next time I suspect myself first.
Next time, use a pencil. Leave the burning to me.
Mom puts the pumpkin in the window. She keeps the smile.
Owning up is the hardest math there is. You solved it.
Then Uncle Gus pokes his head in, grinning.
Mia! Thursday you show me your bike. No training wheels!
Mia goes pale. Into the walkie she whispers: I can't.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
